messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD#INC-4832: missing heartbeat from on-prem agent acme-clinic-02 (customer: Acme Health). Pager routed to rachel (oncall) and SRE escalation.

pagerduty: PD-4832 assigned to rachel (oncall). Auto-escalation schedule active.

rachel (oncall): ack. grabbing context now. Is this isolated to that agent or many agents in the VPC?

marc (sre): quick summary: agent-manager shows repeated DialTimeout to acme-clinic-02 since 12:07 UTC. Other agents in same customer VPC mostly fine. Control-plane logs: "WARN agent acme-clinic-02 missed 3 heartbeats".

emily (netops): running a connectivity probe to acme IP 10.2.16.45: ``nc -vz -w3 10.2.16.45 8443`` -> hangs then times out. Traceroute shows last hop at their virtual appliance, then star.

carla (customer-eng): customer posted they pushed a firewall change at ~12:05 UTC to tighten East-West rules. They're on standby to revert. They've opened a ticket with their network team.

rachel (oncall): marking potential root cause: customer firewall rule change. Impact: control plane cannot reach agent -> partial feature disruption for that customer's Private deployment. Severity: Sev2.

incident-bot: runbook 'private-agent-lost-heartbeat' step 1 executed by rachel. Commands: 1) verify agent heartbeat; 2) attempt management plane to-agent connection; 3) request customer network rollback.

marc (sre): attempted management connection via relay proxy: ``curl -sS https://relay-host.internal/agent-proxy/acme-clinic-02/health`` -> 502 gateway. Relay path also failing to reach agent IP.

emily (netops): provider-bot indicates no TransitGateway flaps on our side. Suspect customer-side firewall. I've DM'd provider contacts for quick route/ACL checks.

carla (customer-eng): customer confirms they added a deny rule for unknown outbound IPs, and after seeing errors they can roll it back. They asked if we can provide the list of control-plane egress IPs to allow.

rachel (oncall): provide IPs from ip-allowlist doc: ``34.201.112.12, 34.201.112.13, 34.201.112.14`` (these are example egress IPs). Also ask for timeframe for rollback.

customer-eng (via carla): customer replies: rollback in progress, ETA 8-10m.

marc (sre): while waiting, attempting a deferred mitigation: enable temporary outbound NAT through our managed relay for this customer (relay-tunnel). Note: this is non-compliant for some customers; must be approved by security. pinging security via thread.

emily (netops): sec-team out for lunch atm. If customer is rolling back quickly, holding on relay enable.

provider-bot: automated note: maintenance window 12:00-12:30 UTC in customer's cloud account showing applied ACL change event by user acme-netops at 12:04 UTC.

carla (customer-eng): customer rolled back rule at 12:14 UTC. Please confirm connectivity.

marc (sre): re-run probe: ``nc -vz -w3 10.2.16.45 8443`` -> succeeded, connection to 10.2.16.45 8443 open. Agent-manager logs show immediate reconnection: ``INFO agent acme-clinic-02 heartbeat resumed at 2026-03-20T12:15:07Z``.

rachel (oncall): confirming with customer.

carla (customer-eng): customer confirms their app is back to normal, no more 503s. They will keep monitoring.

marc (sre): lowering incident severity to monitoring. Logging timeline and adding evidence to incident ticket.

rachel (oncall): handing off to marc for post-incident follow-ups: add a trybook to proactively query provider maintenance windows when pager fires, and consider adding rule-change detection alerting on customer-side ACLs where we have visibility.

marc (sre): taking handoff. Follow-ups: 1) add preflight maintenance check in runbook; 2) document requirement to share egress IP allowlist with customers; 3) explore optional signed tunnel negotiation flow for customers that permit it.

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-4832 resolved at 12:28 UTC (auto-closure by rachel).

carla (customer-eng): customer request: a short RCA email to share with their network team summarizing timeline and suggested guardrails. I'll draft and share.

emily (netops): noted: provider maintenance events should be pulled into our incident context automatically. I'll open a ticket with infra to add the provider webhook.

rachel (oncall): thanks all. no further action required right now. Monitoring for 30m then close incident. :white_check_mark:
